extracted.intended_audience: military lawyers, Army administrators, and adjudicators advising on enlistment and reenlistment law
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and holdings governing who may be enlisted or reenlisted in the U.S. Army, how fraudulent enlistments and convictions affect status, and procedural/contractual consequences (age, citizenship, minors, terms, characterization of service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition options for fraudulent enlistment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a soldier fraudulently enlists (including cases where he had not been discharged from a prior enlistment), the Government may (at its option) bring him to trial for desertion and fraudulent enlistment, restore him to duty without trial and hold him to either the fraudulent enlistment or the prior enlistment, or summarily discharge him without honor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites: P. ^, U2, Oct. 1891; C. 321, Sept. 12, 1894; many opinions (e.g., C. 321, 1894; 4663, 1898). If tried and sentenced by court-martial, it would be unjust to also summarily discharge him (I A 9 g(3), I A 9 i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraudulent enlistment as both criminal and civil (voidable contract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraudulent enlistment has a two-fold character—criminal and civil; in its civil character it is a fraudulent contract which may be avoided, and when avoided the party committing the fraud has no right to benefits of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal consequence: Government may summarily discharge a fraudulently enlisted soldier causing loss of contractual enlistment rights if that is deemed the best disposition instead of trial (I A 9 k; P. 58, 318, Mar. 1893).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of serving under a fraudulent enlistment on discharge character
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a distinction between the fraudulent contract of enlistment and the character of service thereunder; if the contract is not avoided the service is legal and the soldier may be entitled to the discharge his services merit (including honorable discharge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discharge is honorable, it should generally be viewed as establishing that the service was honest and faithful (I A 9 l; citations C. 355, 1894; 2022, 1896).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting time served under fraudulent enlistment toward retirement/continuous service
rubrics_metrics.description: Time actually served under a fraudulent enlistment should be counted in computing service for retirement and toward continuous service, unless the enlistment is voided by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that such time counts toward 30 years necessary for retirement under Sept. 30, 1890 act and toward continuous service unless voided (I A 9 m, I A 9 o; cited cases C. 355, 1894; 16644, 1904; 7108, 1899).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards/pay for service under fraudulent enlistment
rubrics_metrics.description: The award of a certificate of merit and additional pay is lawful for a soldier serving under a fraudulent enlistment if he is restored to duty without trial and merits it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: certificate of merit lawful and additional pay authorized statutes (I A 9 n; C. 16644, July 27, 1904).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary/authority may designate classes ineligible for enlistment
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes permitting enlistment (e.g., for Ordnance Corps) do not prevent the Secretary of War from designating classes (such as married men) from whom enlistment shall not be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held re sec. 1162 R.S.; Secretary has discretion to exclude classes (I A 10; C. 1655, Aug. 13, 1905).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to enlist married men/minors with limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is lawful to give general authority to enlist married men and men with minor children for certain volunteer service (e.g., Volunteer Signal Corps) if statutes permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case holdings authorize Chief Signal Officer to enlist married men/minor-children fathers for Volunteer Signal Corps (I A 11; C. 4208, May 31, 1898).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age limits for first enlistment fixed by statute (18–35) and not waivable
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of March 2, 1899 fixes age limits for original enlistments as 18 to 35 years and it is beyond executive power to waive that limit in a particular case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited opinion: C. 4306, Feb. 8, 1907 (I B 1 a). The act of March 2, 1899 (30 Stat. 978) limits ages for original enlistments to 18–35 (I D 2 c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlistment of minors: guardian consent and custody rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The written consent of the legally appointed guardian is sufficient for a minor's enlistment unless the guardian's authority is restricted; father is natural guardian if living except where custody has been granted to mother by decree; emancipation under state law (e.g., Texas) can permit enlistment without parental consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple holdings: guardian consent required (C. 10040, Aug. 2, 1909); alien minors with parental consent and preliminary naturalization papers may enlist (C. 6726, May 3, 1907); uncle or Indian agent not guardian absent appointment — enlistment violates regulation (C. 184, 1894); Texas emancipation under state civil law valid (C. 22418, Nov. 30, 1907) (I B 1 b and subparts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlistment of aliens/citizenship requirements (peacetime vs war)
rubrics_metrics.description: In time of peace (except Indians) first enlistments are limited to U.S. citizens or those who have made a legal declaration of intention to become citizens; in time of war exceptions may apply and aliens may enlist in Volunteer Army being raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holdings cite act of Aug. 1, 1894 (28 Stat. 216) and its limitation to 'time of peace'; examples include enlistment of Porto Rican, Filipino, and Cuban natives and the requirement that declarations be 'legal declarations' under statute (I C 1 a–g, I C 1 c, I C 1 d, I C 1 e(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalization/declaration must comply with statutory procedures and jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration of intention to become a citizen must be made in accordance with Congress's naturalization statutes; declarations before officials outside the jurisdiction (e.g., in Cuba) are not 'legal declarations' within the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of enlistment statutes and interpretation (regular and volunteer forces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes fix terms: e.g., Aug. 1, 1894 fixes three-year term for Army enlistments; volunteer enlistments in 1898 were for two years or during the war; references to duration of war are restrictions, not extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to Indians as well (no exception); volunteer terms and discharge directives to President do not give individual right to discharge before term (I B 2 a, I B 2 d, I B 2 e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Making good lost time and effect of civil custody on enlistment completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of May 11, 1908 provides that an enlistment is not complete until soldier has made good time lost during enlistment by unauthorized absences exceeding one day; a soldier absent in hands of civil authorities is absent without leave unless acquitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G. 17518, Oct. 2, 1911; failure to make good time can complicate recording of enlistment as complete; neglect by unit clerks may lead to discharge being recorded as complete for convenience of Government (I B 2 b, I B 2 b(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention beyond term for exigency of service vs. lack of statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Soldiers may be retained beyond term in exigencies (e.g., retention until discharge in the U.S. during homeward voyage from Philippines), but there is no authority to retain soldiers beyond term solely for Government convenience absent statutory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holdings: retention proper when based on exigency (C. 13517, 16900, 17700); retaining Philippine Scouts beyond term for exposition lacked authority (C. 16900, Sept. 16, 1904) (I B 2 f, I B 2 g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldier's status while sick awaiting notice of discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier too sick to receive notice of discharge at expiration of term remains in the service awaiting service of notice and his status is one of duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility after conviction/pardon: conviction/pardon effect on enlistment
rubrics_metrics.description: A full and unconditional pardon restores legal rights but does not necessarily restore eligibility to enlist—the fact of a prior conviction or that service was not 'honest and faithful' may still render a person ineligible under statutes like section 1118 R.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: convicted felon pardoned after serving sentence remained ineligible for enlistment (P. 36, 262, Nov. 1889; C. 2769, Nov. 30, 1896). A pardon does not obliterate that prior service was not honest and faithful for purposes of reenlistment (I D 3 c (6), (7), (8), (9)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation excluding persons imprisoned under sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 859, Army Regulations of 1908, prohibits enlistment of a man who has been imprisoned under sentence of a court in a reformatory, jail, or penitentiary; but confinement at the applicant's request to a workhouse without criminal offense may not trigger that prohibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied: applicant sent by his own request to New York workhouse — regulation did not prohibit enlistment (C. 9490, Apr. 2, 1910). Also applied to State Industrial School for Boys cases (C. 9490, Dec. 9, 1911; Jan. 10, 1912) (I B 3 c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and consequences of 'reenlistment' and pay incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Reenlistment can be used narrowly (reenlistment within one month triggering increased pay) but statutes also treat reenlistment as reentry into service without time limitation; reenlistment within statutory short periods may carry additional pay, and Aug. 1, 1894 extended the period to three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 1282/1284 prescribe increased pay for reenlistment within one month; Aug. 1, 1894 extended to three months. Prior naval or Marine service is not counted as Army service for reenlistment age exceptions (I D 1, I D 2 a, I D 2 b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting prior service from other services for reenlistment eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous service in the Navy or as volunteer officers generally does not count as prior Army enlisted service for purposes of reenlistment eligibility and age exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that prior naval or Marine Corps service cannot be counted to make up required length for reenlistment or to overcome age limits for original enlistments (P. 62, 90, Oct. 17, 1893; C. 8758, Dec. 31, 1897; I D 2 a, I D 2 b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of service as 'honest and faithful' and reenlistment
rubrics_metrics.description: Service is presumed honest and faithful if a soldier serves to end of enlistment unless contrary determined by law; character 'not honest and faithful' should not be noted except on approved finding of a board of officers; reenlistment eligibility requires last preceding term to have been honest and faithful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many holdings: being tried/punished by court-martial does not per se render service unfaithful; boards of officers decide characterization; strict interpretation that any offense makes service unfaithful is impracticable—each case decided on merits (I D 3 a, I D 3 a(1), I D 3 c and subparts). Listing numerous precedents showing applications (C. 3036; C. 3756; C. 2158; C. 15119; etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of restoration to duty without trial on reenlistment character
rubrics_metrics.description: A deserter restored to duty without trial may, if his subsequent service continues honest and faithful to the end of his enlistment, be discharged with the remark 'service honest and faithful' and 'no objection known to his reenlistment'; restoration/pardon does not automatically bar consideration of reformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility of persons dropped for desertion or dishonorably discharged
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer dropped from the rolls for desertion is ineligible for reappointment and, under section 1118 R.S., for enlistment or muster into service as a soldier; a dishonorably discharged soldier is generally ineligible for reenlistment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holdings: section 1229 R.S. consequences; multiple citations where dishonorably discharged applicants were held ineligible (I B 3 b; I D 3 c (11) and others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on executing forfeiture by retaining beyond enlistment term
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier sentenced to forfeiture of pay for a term cannot be legally retained beyond his enlistment term solely for the purpose of completing execution of the forfeiture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: forfeiture of $10 per month for 18 months—cannot be held beyond enlistment term to complete forfeiture execution (I B 2 h; R. 16, 94, May 1865).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-case continuance of service where duty prevents reenlistment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where service location or duty (e.g., isolated Alaskan telegraph station seasons) prevents immediate reenlistment, an enlisted man may be discharged and reenlisted or, with his consent in emergency and to prevent interruption, continued in service under his enlistment until he can reach a place for reenlistment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to Signal Corps telegraph stations inaccessible certain seasons; held permissible with consent or discharge and reenlist (C. 19281, Mar. 2, 1906; C. 16900, 1904; C. 17700, 1905) (I B 2 c).
